Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-18
Time: 3:00 PM EST
Duration: ~55 minutes
Recording: yes

Summary: quick product walkthrough focused on model scouting playbooks, compatibility matrices, and benchmark interpretation; customer evaluating Hosted vs Dedicated for latency-sensitive underwriting tasks; discussed cost/latency tradeoffs, quantization, and audit/compliance items.

Topics: Playbook-driven scouting, benchmark spreadsheet walkthrough, kernel/runtime compatibility, Dedicated sandbox, security/compliance ask list.

Action items (auto): Alex to send benchmark sheet; Priya to spin up Dedicated sandbox; Customer to send prompt sets.

Transcript:
[00:00] Alex (AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Alex Morgan from Redwood, AE. With me is Priya Patel, our solutions engineer. 
[00:10] Priya (SE): Hi! Hello. Thanks for having us, excited to go through the playbook flow today.
[00:15] Samira (BlueHarbor): Hi Alex, Priya. Samira here. We also have Ethan and Linda. Linda might need to drop at 3:40.
[00:22] Ethan (BlueHarbor): Hey all. Platform side — I'll be focused on perf, infra, and the Dedicated questions.
[00:27] Linda (BlueHarbor): Hi, quick context — we're evaluating for claims-underwriting and a new fraud-detection assistant. Latency is a big deal for quick decisions.
[00:36] Alex: Great, quick agenda: 1) show model catalog scouting/playbook in Console, 2) demo bench spreadsheet + how to interpret results, 3) discuss compatibility matrix and kernel mapping, and 4) next steps for a POC. Sound good?
[00:46] Samira: Yes. Also want to hear about data residency and SOC 2 stuff — that will come up in procurement.
[00:52] Priya: We'll cover the security checklist briefly at the end, yes.

[02:00] Priya: (sharing) So here's the Console — this is the playbook tab. The idea is you define workload profiles — in your case low-latency underwriting with typical prompt length, and a second profile for multi-turn fraud investigation which is longer context.
[02:15] Priya: We show candidate open models with columns: throughput, median token latency at 128/512 context, quantization friendliness, and kernel compatibility per GPU family.
[02:30] Ethan: Can you show how you mark a model as "compatible" with our on-prem A100 cluster? We have mixed gen A100 and H100 scheduled next quarter.
[02:40] Priya: Sure — compatibility is a matrix. For A100 we flag optimized kernels and note if we need 4-bit quant or special kernels for attention. You'll see a green/yellow/red flag and notes like "KV cache mem spikes at 2K tokens if unquantized" — those are observed in our bench runs.
[03:05] Alex: Also important: the playbook can pin a fallback model for when resources are constrained — so you get consistent latency SLOs.

[04:00] Samira: About the bench spreadsheet — what inputs do you need from us to make it actionable?
[04:08] Alex: Good question — three things: representative prompt suites, target latency SLOs, and a sample throughput profile (reqs/sec). With that we run per-model microbenchmarks and provide cost/latency per 1k requests.
[04:23] Samira: We have both short prompts for underwriting and long context for audit trails. We'll provide 600 prompts total across both.
[04:29] Alex: Perfect.

[05:00] Priya: (walkthrough) Here's a bench result row — model name (open-3b-quant), median tail p95 tokens/sec, cost per 1M tokens assuming Dedicated pricing, and a compatibility note. You'll notice we also include a recommended quant profile (nf4, int8, etc) and estimated quality delta after quantization.
[05:25] Ethan: How reliable are those quality deltas? For us a slight drop in NER is sensitive for claims classification.
[05:33] Priya: We run small eval sets — they'll give a delta estimate but it's probabilistic. We also include a regression alert step you can enable in Redwood Optimize that will monitor eval metrics against your golden prompts once live.
[05:50] Linda: Is that part of Redwood Optimize or Console?
[05:53] Alex: It's in Optimize, but surfaced in Console as suggestions. Think of Console for discovery and Optimize for ongoing tuning.

[07:10] Ethan: For Dedicated, do we get kernel-level visibility? We need to know which kernels are used for attention and if we can pin them for stability across updates.
[07:20] Priya: Yes — in Dedicated you can see kernel mapping per model version and runtime. You can pin a kernel bundle to avoid changes during a rollout. We also provide a kernels changelog.
[07:33] Samira: What about auto-fallback? If H100 runs out, can traffic go to a CPU quantized variant in a different region?
[07:42] Priya: Yep. Smart routing policies let you prefer latency region then fallback to cost tier. You can set hard SLOs and Redwood will route to a variant that meets them if available, otherwise it will use the most cost-effective compatible fallback and flag the request.

[09:00] Alex: Quick aside: common misconception is "more params == better accuracy for all tasks". Our playbooks help pick right-size models for your workload to reduce cost while meeting quality.
[09:15] Samira: That's important. For underwriting, we don't need huge open models; we need stable entity extraction and factual recall.

[10:00] Priya: Demo: I'll filter the catalog for models that have high NER on our evals and are marked as 'stable quant'. See how the compatibility matrix updates by hardware family.
[10:20] Priya: (typical transcription glitch) This model has a note — "behaves odd on long sequences, recommended batch size 4" — the console shows a link to the bench run.
[10:35] Ethan: Can we run custom bench runs ourselves from the Console against our payload to validate?
[10:40] Priya: Yes, via the Bench tab — you can upload your prompt suite, select models and target infra (Hosted / Dedicated), and kick off runs. You get per-run logs and flamegraphs for perf hotspots.

[12:00] Linda: Security questions: data residency, audit logs, SSO, and key rotation.
[12:08] Alex: Short answers — Private deployments give you VPC and on-prem options and customer-managed KMS. We ship audit logs for every token request in Dedicated + Private, and Console supports SAML SSO and RBAC. We'll share the full security pack.
[12:25] Linda: Do you have SOC 2 Type II?
[12:28] Alex: Yes, SOC 2 Type II, ISO attestation listed in our security pack. We'll kick that to you after the call.

[14:00] Samira: On cost: show me an example tradeoff — like a 1M token/month profile using open-3b-quant vs open-13b.
[14:10] Priya: (shares) Here's a cost-per-1M tokens row — open-3b-quant is ~1/4th the token cost of open-13b on Dedicated with nf4 quant, and median latency is 60ms vs 240ms under similar batching. We also show delta in eval score — for your NER test delta is ~1.5%.
[14:35] Ethan: That 1.5% might be acceptable if it reduces cost; we need to see how it affects downstream recall.

[16:00] Alex: Recap on the playbook workflow: 1) define workload profiles, 2) run bench with your prompts, 3) pick shortlist and assign kernels/quant profiles, 4) enable fallback and rollout policies, 5) monitor via Optimize for regressions.
[16:25] Samira: Sounds good. We like the idea of starting Hosted quick-check then Dedicated sandbox for the critical path.

[18:00] Priya: One more demo piece — compatibility export. You can export a CSV of the compatibility matrix and it includes model, recommended quant, kernel notes, and a suggested route policy YAML you can import into infra.
[18:18] Ethan: That YAML import will be handy for our infra automation.

[20:00] Samira: Any pitfalls you commonly see during POCs?
[20:05] Alex: Yup — mismatched prompt realism (customers test with toy prompts), not pinning kernels during canary, and ignoring tail latency outliers. We provide a POC checklist to avoid these.
[20:18] Samira: Please send that.
[20:20] Alex: Will do.

[22:00] (brief demo glitch) Priya: sorry, Console lagging a bit. There may be a transcription typo there — shows a weird label "quant punkt" in the run notes, that should read "quant punt" — our bad.
[22:15] Samira: Haha, no worries.

[24:00] Linda: I need to drop in a few. Final asks: can you enumerate the security artifacts you'll send and the timeline?
[24:10] Alex: We'll send: SOC 2 report, data processing addendum (DPA), network diagrams for Private deployment, and our KMS integration guide. Expect those by 2026-11-20.
[24:25] Linda: Great.

[26:00] Priya: Next steps recap: Alex shares bench template and pricing; Priya configures Dedicated sandbox and will invite Ethan; Samira sends prompts; we'll reconvene with security + procurement present.
[26:18] Samira: Okay. Who owns scheduling the POC scoping call?
[26:22] Alex: I'll set that up — look for a calendar invite.

[30:00] (wrap up) Alex: Anything else?
[30:03] Ethan: One more technical — how do you handle KV cache eviction with multi-tenant Dedicated pods?
[30:10] Priya: We give two modes: per-customer isolated cache, or shared cache with namespace-based eviction. For Dedicated you typically choose isolated to avoid cross-tenant pollution.
[30:22] Ethan: Good.

[32:00] Linda: dropping now, thanks all.
[32:05] Samira: Thanks.
[33:00] Alex: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the artifacts and invite Ethan to the sandbox.

(Transcript ends — note: automated captions imperfect; some proper nouns may be spelled incorrectly)
